extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting preprints in archaeology, anthropology, and related human-environment fields to PCI Archaeology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting archaeology-related preprints for evaluation and recommendation by the PCI Archaeology community, including editorial standards, reproducibility rules, ethical requirements, formatting and data-deposition instructions, and the evaluation workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scientific, methodological, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology recommends only preprints that meet high scientific, methodological, and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders select work that stands out for its context, questions, methods, or findings; recommended articles should be 'remarkable' and as close to perfect as possible in form because a recommended article is a finished article. Preprints must not be published or under review elsewhere when submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory data and code sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must share raw data, code, and analysis scripts with reviewers at submission and make them available to readers after recommendation (except for ethical reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits should be in open repositories (e.g., Zenodo, Dryad, institutional repo) with a DOI or other permanent identifier (e.g., SWHID). Raw data, scripts, and codes must be carefully described so another researcher can reuse them; Git URLs are not permanent. README files explaining data/scripts/code are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details on quantitative analyses and simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must provide details on quantitative analyses (data treatment and statistical scripts) and details concerning simulations (scripts, codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scripts or correctly versioned deposits in an open repository with a DOI or permanent identifier. Scripts or codes must be carefully described such that another researcher can run them; include program installation instructions and annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear justification of sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to provide a clear justification of sample sizes in empirical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications should address statistical power, Bayes factor thresholds, or estimate precision for quantitative studies, and information power or saturation thresholds for qualitative studies. See Lakens (2022) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide experimental procedure details
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on experimental procedures must be given in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should be sufficiently detailed to allow replication; for specimen-based studies provide complete repository information and institutional abbreviations if applicable; specimens must be deposited in an accessible and permanent repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of preregistration, replications, and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology welcomes replications, preregistered research, and well-designed studies reporting negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to post preregistrations and may submit preregistrations to PCI Registered Reports. Replication studies are assessed using the same criteria provided the article is interesting to a recommender.

rubrics_metrics.name: No financial conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions with financial conflicts of interest are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the PCI code of conduct. Authors should declare any potential non-financial conflict of interest; recommenders and reviewers must be free from conflicts of interest related to the study or its authors as far as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology evaluates preprints dealing with all fields of archaeology, anthropology, and human-environment interactions worldwide since the appearance of human cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes all disciplines and methods that enhance knowledge about the human past. Preregistrations should go to PCI Registered Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only papers written in English will be considered for recommendation in PCI Archaeology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic translation of abstracts and keywords is offered to improve discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage policy — permitted editorial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Using AI to translate, correct or improve text or software code is allowed provided authors review/approve/check the production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This use is similar to using traditional language correction services and poses no problem as soon as the authors verify and approve the output.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage policy — AI for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Using AI to analyse bibliography or data is acceptable if such methods have been published and are properly cited or are original and sufficiently detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data analysis using AI is not intrinsically different from other analytical methods but must be transparent and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI authorship prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Artificial intelligence cannot be considered an author of an article submitted to PCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All people listed as authors must meet authorship criteria (ICMJE 2017): substantial contribution, draft/critically revise, approve final version, and agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI disclosure and prohibition of AI-generated illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: When AI is used to generate text and code, authors must disclose how they used AI in methods or acknowledgements; authors must not generate illustrations using AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must carefully check for plagiarism, hallucinations, or other errors when using AI. Non-compliance may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and intellectual property vigilance with AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, reviewers and recommenders must ensure no part of the manuscript has been published elsewhere and that AI-generated content does not infringe existing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can reproduce material similar to training data; check for plagiarism and cite sources appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint posting before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should first post their article on a preprint server or open-access repository before submitting to PCI Archaeology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After posting, use the 'Submit preprint' button; for anonymous submissions follow separate instructions (see anonymous submission) involving private interfaces rather than public preprint servers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition timing and permanence of supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data, statistical scripts, pipeline scripts, simulation code and supplementary information must be available to reviewers at submission and to readers after recommendation via a correctly versioned deposit with a DOI or permanent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After recommendation materials must be available in the text or through repositories like Zenodo, Dryad, etc. Git URLs are not permanent; guidance for issuing a DOI for GitHub is provided. Data/scripts must be described so others can reuse them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and acceptable secondary publication
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of the manuscript has been published, except for passages that are properly cited; original data must be clearly distinguished from published data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All extracted information from other publications must be provided with citations; consent must be obtained for unpublished data cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: All people listed as authors must meet the authorship criteria: substantial contributions, wrote or critically revised the MS, approved final version, and agreed to be accountable (ICMJE 2017); all listed authors must be aware and have agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person who meets authorship criteria should be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical experimentation and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving human participants should meet the Declaration of Helsinki; animal studies should follow Consensus Author Guidelines on Animal Ethics and Welfare and have ethical review committee approval where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include a statement that informed consent was obtained for human subjects. Ensure necessary approvals before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabrication, manipulation, or biased interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the data presented should be fabricated or distorted; images must not be manipulated to mislead; study results must be interpreted objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors discover any serious error before or after recommendation they will alert PCI Archaeology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements and consent for cited/unpublished materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All non-author contributors should be mentioned in Acknowledgements and must have agreed to be mentioned; owners of copyright for previously published figures/tables must agree to inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent should be obtained from authors of any unpublished data cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources of funding for the study must be listed in a separate funding section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit: list all funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure format
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should declare any potential non-financial conflict of interest; financial conflicts are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no competing interests, include the template sentence confirming compliance with the PCI rule of having no financial conflicts; if recommenders are authors, indicate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting basics to facilitate peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Although no strict word limits, authors are requested to follow guidelines: lines numbered, tables and figures in main text, define abbreviations (except obvious ones), and pay attention to typographical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommended article is a finished article; text should be cohesive, logically organized, and easy to follow. Check presence of tables/figures, accessibility of data/scripts, and accuracy of references. Use provided Word and LaTeX templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be as concise as possible but as long as necessary to ensure rationale and methods are clear and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow formatting conventions of their discipline and note any later journal-specific limits if they plan to submit elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be unambiguous, understandable to specialists in other fields, and reflect the content of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make title accessible to cross-disciplinary specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Authors and contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate full name and affiliation of each author; provide e-mail addresses (at least corresponding author and first authors if different); authors are invited to indicate ORCID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anonymous submissions, authors' names go into the submission form but are hidden from recommended reviewers and suggested recommenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract should be concise and present the main findings of the study; structured abstracts can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract clearly communicates main results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction should clearly explain the reasons for the study, build on relevant recent and past research, and clearly present the research question/hypothesis/prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly situate the study within the literature and state objectives/hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Materials and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials and methods must provide sufficient detail to allow replication; details of experimental procedures and quantitative analyses must be fully available either in the text or through deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include repository information for specimens; ensure scripts and code allow reproduction of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be described and interpreted correctly; data must be available to readers in the article or through deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For negative results include appropriate statistical power or Bayesian/equivalence analyses as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure — Discussion and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion should answer the research questions, compare main results with published data objectively, emphasize strengths and limitations, and conclusions must be clearly stated and supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretations are allowed but must be clearly identified as such and not overstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and tables should be located in the main text and be easily understandable without reference to the main body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions must be informative but concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and citation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to use their preferred reference style but APA 7 is suggested; DOIs should be provided if available; author-year or numerical schemes acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All references cited in text must be included in the reference list; follow DORA by citing original research as primary source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process — recommenders suggested
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission authors will be asked to suggest between 5 and 10 recommenders who could handle evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders are similar to journal editors; they find reviewers, collect reviews, and make editorial decisions. PCI is not obliged to consider every submission; if no recommender acts within 20 days authors will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit anonymously (double-blind) by NOT depositing on a public preprint server and instead using a private web interface, depositing data/scripts in the same or another private interface, and indicating anonymity in the submission form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT indicate names in the cover letter; authors still list names in the submission form visible to Managing Board but not to suggested recommenders or reviewers. If recommended, authors must deposit a final non-anonymized version in an open archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation workflow — minimum reviews and recommender role
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommender handling a preprint will invite reviewers to obtain at least two high-quality reviews; classic cycles of reviews/decision/author response may follow, and recommenders sign decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each round recommender may reject, recommend, or request revisions. Median time to first decision is 45 days. If recommended, the recommender writes a recommendation text published with all editorial correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent review publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology publishes all reviews of recommended manuscripts (reviewers may choose to sign or remain anonymous) and publishes all reviews and recommender decision letters at acceptance; reviews of rejected submissions are not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and recommenders must adhere to the PCI code of conduct; abusive reviews may be edited, returned, or discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling manuscripts by recommenders — conflict declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders who handle manuscripts must declare that they have no conflict of interest of any kind with the content or authors of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only preprints that attract the interest of at least one qualified recommender are sent for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for rejected manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of rejected manuscripts can appeal within 30 days by contacting PCI Archaeology; appeals are considered by the specialist recommender(s) and the Managing Board and decisions are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals email: contact@archaeo.peercommunityin.org

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment questionnaire for manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to self-assess using questions about title/abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, and discussion to facilitate smoother evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Does the title reflect content? Does abstract present main findings? Are methods sufficiently detailed to allow replication? Are conclusions supported by results?

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment checklist for data, scripts, and code
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist: Can data and script be accessed via links? Is a README present? Are metadata and annotations available? Are files comprehensible? Do scripts function and generate matching results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent errors to fix include missing script verification, scripts referencing mismatched file names, absolute paths vs relative paths, non-English script comments, poor README, lack of installation instructions, insufficient script annotations, omission of execution time commentary, non-preconfigured package installs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable data and citation of DOIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible, data, scripts, codes, and supplementary information should be provided in machine-readable formats and avoid PDFs for data; if DOIs/URLs are used they must be cited in the text and reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct versioning and permanent identifiers; include README files to make materials understandable and reusable.
